Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow. American literature has undergone a profound transformation from its early colonial roots to its present-day complexity. The initial literary works, often theological in nature, reflected the Puritan settlers’ rigid worldview, emphasising moral rectitude and divine providence. Writers such as Jonathan Edwards and Anne Bradstreet used their prose and poetry to navigate religious devotion and personal introspection. However, as the colonies moved towards independence, literature took on a more political tone, with figures like Thomas Paine and Benjamin Franklin using rhetorical finesse to galvanise revolutionary sentiment.The 19th century marked a period of literary expansion, as American authors sought to carve a distinct identity apart from European influences. Romanticism flourished with writers like Nathaniel Hawthorne and Edgar Allan Poe, whose works explored psychological depth, human fallibility and gothic sensibilities. Simultaneously, transcendentalists such as Ralph Waldo Emerson and Henry David Thoreau championed individualism and nature’s spiritual significance. By the latter half of the century, realism emerged as a counterpoint to romantic idealism, with Mark Twain and Henry James depicting life’s intricacies through meticulous detail and social critique.The 20th century saw American literature fracture into numerous stylistic and thematic branches. Modernist writers like TS Eliot and William Faulkner experimented with fragmented narratives and stream-of-consciousness techniques, reflecting the disillusionment of a rapidly changing world. The Harlem Renaissance brought forth voices such as Langston Hughes, who redefined African American identity in literature. In the postmodern era, figures like Thomas Pynchon and Don DeLillo interrogated the nature of truth, media and technological encroachment on human experience.American literature continues to evolve, encapsulating diverse perspectives and experimental forms. It serves not only as a reflection of historical and cultural shifts but also as an ever-adapting narrative of the American consciousness.Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘rectitude’ as used in the passage.

Comprehension:Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. By mid-2025, the global water crisis is expected to reach unprecedented levels. According to the 2024 UN World Water Development Report, approximately 2.2 billion people lack access to safely managed drinking water, and 3.5 billion lack safely managed sanitation services. Meanwhile, nearly half of the world’s population experiences severe water scarcity for at least part of each year. Agriculture consumes about 70% of global freshwater withdrawals, while industry and municipal use account for roughly 20% and 12%, respectively. Climate change is further destabilizing the hydrological cycle. Rising temperatures, glacial melt, and changing precipitation patterns are reducing freshwater availability, while floods and droughts increase in frequency and severity. Coastal aquifers face growing salinization: studies show that by 2100, as much as 77% of coastal aquifers could be affected by saltwater intrusion due to sea-level rise and declining recharge. Water scarcity today already affects 40% of the global population, and demand is expected to surpass supply by 40% by 2030. Groundwater depletion continues, especially in densely populated regions like India, China, and Pakistan, where aquifer recharge lags behind extraction. Many megacities now face “Day Zero” scenarios, where municipal taps could run dry without drastic conservation and infrastructure reform. While innovative technologies—such as biodegradable hydrogels that extract water from the air—offer promise for remote or water-stressed regions, current investments fall significantly short of what's needed (a shortfall of $85 billion per year) to achieve universal access by 2030. Experts warn that without coordinated global investment, transparent governance, equitable distribution, and water-efficient infrastructure, the world risks escalating conflict, agricultural collapse, economic instability, and public health crises on a global scale.What real-world connection applies?
options: Water stress affects food security, conflict, and health globally
Scarcity is confined to small islands only
Climate has no impact on water access
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'B' (Water stress affects food security, conflict, and health globally) है।

Comprehension:Read the following passage carefully and choose the best answer to each question out of the four alternatives.Among the most pressing environmental issues in India is also water pollution. The Asian country has experienced unprecedented urban expansion and economic growth in recent years. This, however, comes with huge environmental costs. Besides its air, the country’s waterways have become extremely polluted, with around 70% of surface water estimated to be unfit for consumption. The illegal dumping of raw sewage, silt, and garbage into rivers and lakes severely contaminated India’s waters. The near-total absence of pipe planning and an inadequate waste management system are only exacerbating the situation. Every day, a staggering 40 million litres of wastewater enter rivers and other water bodies. Of these, only a tiny fraction is adequately treated due to a lack of adequate infrastructure.In middle-income countries like India, water pollution can account for the loss of up to half of GDP growth, a World Bank report suggests. Water pollution costs the Indian government between US$6.7 and $7.7 billion a year and is associated with a 9% drop in agricultural revenues as well as a 16% decrease in downstream agricultural yields.Besides affecting humans, with nearly 40 million Indians suffering from waterborne diseases like typhoid, cholera, and hepatitis and nearly 400,000 fatalities each year, water pollution also damages crops, as infectious bacteria and diseases in the water used for irrigation prevent them from growing. Inevitably, freshwater biodiversity is also severely damaged. The country’s rivers and lakes often become open sewers for residential and industrial waste.What is the synonym of the word ‘ unprecedented ‘ from the passage?

Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.The study of ancient civilisations provides valuable insights into human history, offering a window into the lives of people who lived thousands of years ago. Archaeological discoveries have shed light on the daily lives and customs of ancient peoples, revealing how they lived, worked and interacted with their environment. These findings help us understand the development of cultures and societies, showing us the evolution of human civilisation over time. For instance, the excavation of ancient cities has uncovered artifacts such as tools, pottery and inscriptions that tell us about the technological advancements, trade practices and social structures of these societies.However, interpreting these artifacts can be challenging due to limited information. Often, archaeologists must piece together incomplete records and fragmented objects to form a coherent picture of the past. This process requires a great deal of expertise and often involves making educated guesses based on the available evidence. The context in which an artifact is found can significantly influence its interpretation, and without a complete understanding of this context, our conclusions may be tentative or subject to revision.Ongoing research and technological advances continue to reveal new aspects of ancient civilisations. Modern techniques such as radiocarbon dating, DNA analysis and remote sensing have revolutionised the field of archaeology, allowing researchers to obtain more precise and detailed information about ancient peoples and their environments.What is the central theme of the passage?
options: Gaining insights from the past and overcoming interpretive challenges
The technological superiority of modern civilisations over ancient ones
The need for more funding in archaeological research
The importance of studying mythical narratives and cultural practices
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'A' (Gaining insights from the past and overcoming interpretive challenges) है।

questions.question: Comprehension:गद्यांश पर आधारित निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए इस संबंध में एक बात और ध्यान देने योग्य हैं। जिस प्रकार बाह्य शारीरिक कुरूपता मनुष्य के सौंदर्य बोध को कुंठित नहीं कर देती, प्रत्युत कभी- कभी और अधिक तीव्रता दे देती है, उसी प्रकार उसके बाह्य या अंतर्जगत की अपूर्णता उसे पूर्णता का सौंदर्य देखने से नहीं रोकती। ऐसा कुत्सित मनुष्य मिलना कठिन होगा, जिसके अंतर्जगत से पूर्णता की प्रत्येक रेखा मिट गई हो, सामंजस्य के सब रंग धूल गए हों।  साधारणतया घोर मिथ्यावादी भी सत्य को सबसे अधिक सम्मान देता है। मालिनतम व्यक्ति भी पवित्रता का सबसे अधिक मूल्य निश्चित करता है।  मनुष्य संसार के सामने ही नहीं, हृदय के एकांत कोने में भी यह नहीं स्वीकार करना चाहता कि वह मिथ्या के लिए ही मिथ्यावादी है, मलिनता के प्रेम के कारण ही मलिन है। प्रायः वह सब व्यक्तिगत अपूर्णताओं और विषमताओं का भार परिस्थिति पर डालकर, अंतर्जगत में प्रतिष्ठित किसी पूर्णता और सामंजस्य की प्रतिमा के निकट अपने आपको क्षम्य सिद्ध कर लेता है।  यह अपूर्णता से पूर्णता, यथार्थ से आदर्श और भौतिकता से सूक्ष्म तत्त्वों तक विस्तृत जीवन, काव्य और कलाओं की उसी परिधि से घिर सकता है जो सौंदर्य की विविधता से लेकर सत्य की असीम एकरूपता तक फैली हुई है। निम्नलिखित में से मलिन का पर्यायवाची शब्द बताइए
